title: A solvable subgroup through a split maximal torus lies in a regular limit subgroup
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $G$ be a reductive $k$-group [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sfb-reductive-torus-centralizer-terminology], and let $T\subseteq G$ be a split maximal torus [def-sfb-tori-multiplicative-type]. Reductive means smooth affine of finite type, geometrically connected, with no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup after algebraic closure [def-weil-algebraic-closure]; unipotent means that geometric points are unipotent matrices in a faithful representation [def-sfb-solvable-group-structure]. Let $V\subseteq G$ be a smooth connected solvable closed subgroup containing $T$ [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]; solvable means that successive scheme-theoretic commutator subgroups become trivial. No maximality assumption on $V$ is imposed. Put $\Phi=\{\alpha
e0:\operatorname{Lie}(G)_\alpha
e0\}$, where $\operatorname{Lie}(G)$ is the tangent space at the identity and the subscript denotes the character-weight summand of the conjugation representation of $T$. A character is a group homomorphism $T	o\mathbf G_m$, and a cocharacter is a group homomorphism $\mathbf G_m	o T$ [def-sc-gm-ga]. Then there exists a cocharacter $\lambda$ defined over $k$ such that $\alpha\circ\lambda(t)=t^{n_\alpha}$ with $n_\alpha
e0$ for every $\alpha\in\Phi$, and
$$V\subseteq P_\lambda$$
as subgroup functors, where $P_\lambda(A)$ consists of those $g\in G(A)$ for which $t\mapsto\lambda(t)g\lambda(t)^{-1}$ extends from $\mathbf G_{m,A}$ to a morphism $\mathbf A^1_A	o G_A$. If $\Phi=\varnothing$, the assertion includes $\lambda=0$.

source.place: Theorem 21.32 and Corollary 21.33, printed pp.434-435, together with Proposition 21.29, pp.433-434. Applied to a Borel containing the scalar extension of V to an algebraic closure: all geometric Borels through the split torus descend and are regular cocharacter limit subgroups. This is a containment input without a Borel or maximality hypothesis on V.

proof.text: Put $K=\bar k$. The field-extension assertions of [lem-sfb-solvable-normal-subgroup-products] make $V_K$ smooth, connected and solvable. The group $G_K$ is reductive by the geometric hypothesis on $G$. By [lem-sfb-maximal-torus-field-extension], $T_K$ is maximal in $G_K$, and $T_K\subseteq V_K$. Thus all the algebraically closed-field hypotheses needed below hold.

Among the smooth connected solvable closed subgroups of $G_K$ containing $V_K$, choose $B$ with largest dimension. This collection is nonempty (it contains $V_K$), and its dimensions are integers bounded by $\dim G_K$. A proper smooth connected overgroup of $B$ has strictly larger dimension by [lem-sfb-solvable-normal-subgroup-products]. Consequently $B$ is maximal among smooth connected solvable subgroups, hence is a Borel, and $T_K\subseteq V_K\subseteq B$.

source.place: Definition 17.6 and the maximum-dimension observation, pp.353--354

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-regular-cocharacter-borel-description] to $(G_K,T_K,B)$. It gives a cocharacter $\mu:\mathbf G_{m,K}\to T_K$ regular for the nonzero character weights of $\operatorname{Lie}(G_K)$ and $B=P_\mu$. If there are no such weights, its last clause permits the choice $\mu=0$ and gives $G_K=T_K=P_0$.

By the antiequivalence and scalar-extension compatibility in [lem-sfb-multiplicative-character-antiduality], homomorphisms between the split tori $\mathbf G_m$ and $T$ identify with homomorphisms $X^*(T)\to\mathbf Z$, over both $k$ and $K$. Their Galois actions are trivial because the tori are split. Hence scalar extension gives a bijection on these Hom sets. The lattice homomorphism $\mu^*$ therefore defines a $k$-cocharacter $\lambda$ with $\lambda_K=\mu$. It is the zero cocharacter when $\mu=0$.

source.place: Theorem 12.9 and the split-case paragraph of the proof of Corollary 12.25, pp.233,240

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-relative-tangent-weight-base-change] with $A=k$, $B=K$ and a splitting $T\simeq\mathbf G_m^r$. It identifies each geometric character-weight space with $K\otimes_k\operatorname{Lie}(G)_\alpha$. Tensoring a vector space with a field extension preserves and detects nonzeroness, so the nonzero weights are exactly the scalar extensions of $\Phi$. Character antiduality identifies their pairings with $\lambda$ and $\mu$. Thus $n_\alpha=\langle\alpha_K,\mu\rangle\ne0$ for every $\alpha\in\Phi$, with $\alpha\circ\lambda(t)=t^{n_\alpha}$; if $\Phi$ is empty, the preceding zero choice applies.

source.place: Chapter 13 weight decompositions; Definition 21.26, p.433; split character pairing of Chapter 12

proof.text: The field-extension clause of [lem-sfb-reductive-cocharacter-parabolic-geometry] gives a closed subgroup $P_\lambda\subseteq G$ and $(P_\lambda)_K=P_\mu$. Thus $V_K\subseteq B=(P_\lambda)_K$. Write $G=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $V=\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$, and $P_\lambda=\operatorname{Spec}(R/J)$. This inclusion says that every element of $J$ maps to zero in $(R/I)\otimes_k K$. The map $R/I\to(R/I)\otimes_k K$ is injective (extend any nonzero vector to a $k$-basis), hence $J\subseteq I$. The quotient map $R/J\to R/I$ gives $V\subseteq P_\lambda$ as closed subgroup schemes, and therefore on every test algebra, including nonreduced ones.

source.place: Definitions and field-extension compatibility of limit subgroups, pp.263--266; Corollary 21.33, p.435, descent of the resulting containment

proof_origin.place: Definition 17.6 (pp.353--354), Theorem 21.32 and Corollary 21.33 (pp.434--435), with split Hom invariance from the proof of Corollary 12.25 (p.240). The descent and weight checks are written out explicitly.

Source check: I read Milne iAG2017 Def. 21.26, Prop. 21.29, Thm. 21.32 and Cor. 21.33 (pp. 433-435); the six steps follow that argument, applied to a geometric Borel that contains V_K. Step 1: the field-extension clauses of solvable-normal-subgroup-products and maximal-torus-field-extension give V_K smooth, connected and solvable and T_K maximal; G_K is reductive by hypothesis. The two nodes define solvable differently (derived series versus a normal series), but def-sfb-solvable-group-structure states that the two are equivalent, so this is elementary. Step 2 chooses B of maximum dimension among the overgroups of V_K; the strict-dimension clause shows B is a Borel in the borel-description node's sense. Step 3 applies the converse clause of regular-cocharacter-borel-description over K to get B = P(mu); when Phi is empty, mu = 0 and P(0) = G. Step 4 uses split antiduality with base-change compatibility: scalar extension is a bijection on Hom(G_m, T), so mu = lambda_K for a k-cocharacter lambda into T itself. Step 5 uses relative-tangent-weight-base-change with A = k and B = K: the weights over K are the extensions of Phi, so n_alpha = <alpha_K, mu> is nonzero. Step 6 uses parabolic-geometry: P_lambda is closed and its formation commutes with field extension, and injectivity of R/I -> (R/I) tensor K gives J contained in I, so V lies in P_lambda on all algebras. Edge cases checked: G = T of any rank including 0, V = T, upper and lower Borels of SL_2 (mu must be chosen from B), finite and imperfect fields. lean.statement: theorem splitTorus_solvable_cocharacter_containment {k : Type u} [Field k] (G T V : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))) (hG : ReductiveTorusCentralizer.IsReductive G) (i : T ⟶ G) (hT : ReductiveTorusCentralizer.IsMaximalTorus i) (hSplit : ∃ r : ℕ, Nonempty (T ≅ MultiplicativeType.splitTorus k r)) (j : V ⟶ G) (hV : IsClosedSubgroupScheme j.hom.hom) [Smooth V.X.hom] [ConnectedSpace V.X.left] (hSolvable : SolvableGroupStructure.IsSolvable V) (tV : T ⟶ V) (hTV : tV ≫ j = i) : ∃ lam : Grp.mk (StandardGroupSchemes.multiplicative k) ⟶ T, (∀ chi : T ⟶ Grp.mk (StandardGroupSchemes.multiplicative k), chi.hom.hom ≠ 1 → (∃ v : GrpObj.Lie G.X, v ≠ 0 ∧ v ∈ AdjointCharacter.weightVectors i chi) → ∃ n : ℤ, n ≠ 0 ∧ lam.hom.hom ≫ chi.hom.hom = (𝟙 (StandardGroupSchemes.multiplicative k)) ^ n) ∧ (∀ (A : CommAlgCat.{u} k) (v : StandardGroupSchemes.affine k A ⟶ V.X), v ≫ j.hom.hom ∈ CocharacterLimit.parabolicPoints (lam ≫ i) A) ∧ ((¬ ∃ (chi : T ⟶ Grp.mk (StandardGroupSchemes.multiplicative k)) (v : GrpObj.Lie G.X), chi.hom.hom ≠ 1 ∧ v ≠ 0 ∧ v ∈ AdjointCharacter.weightVectors i chi) → lam.hom.hom = 1)
